To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a pause response in a cerebellar Purking cell is a driver of conditioned blink responses and that the pause response is a memory trace that is formed during training and that is expressed during the expression phase.

(1) The learned Purkinje-cell pause response is the main driver of the learned conditioned blink; (2) the pause response is triggered by a learned increase in the excitatory drive to the cerebellar nucleus from the cerebellar cortex; (3) the learned pause response is triggered only when the excitatory drive is sufficiently strong, and (4) this threshold is set by the Purkinje cell’s intrinsic properties, which are determined by its membrane properties and the strength and

the Purkinje cell conditioned pause response, which is a learned cellular event, is the memory trace of the conditioned blink and that this cellular event is the main driver of the conditioned blink response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying learning and memory, in particular classical or Pavlovain conditioning of the blink reflex.
the neural basis of classical conditioning.
the neural mechanisms of learning and memory and the role of the cerebellum in learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Purkinje cell conditioned pause response is the driver of the conditioned blink and the memory trace of classical conditioning.
a learned Purkinje-cell pause response to the conditioning stimulus is the main driver of the conditioned blink and that the pause response is the Pavlovian conditioned memory trace.
the Purkinje cell is the memory trace for classical conditioning of blink responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
classical conditioning is a form of associative learning in which the cerebellum is a key structure.
the Purkinje cell is a memory cell.
the Purkinje cell is a key element in the neural network that controls conditioned responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cerebellum has a role as a memory store and that it does so by storing the memory trace in the form of a pause response in Purkinje cells.
the cerebellum is a key structure for learning and memory.
we propose a mechanism for how learning occurs in a specific circuit and that the learning is stored in the circuit.
